last_full_audit_result: 7 full rounds + 1 scoped. total: 48,22,11,13,14,8,10. WRONG: 13,5,1,1,4,1,3. All confirmed findings fixed each round. CONCLUSION (strong): neither total=0 NOR WRONG=0 is a reachable/provable fixed point of (sweep→doc-fix→sweep). Two structural reasons proven empirically: (1) finders are NON-DETERMINISTIC — each round samples a different ~10-deep slice, so latent errors surface stochastically (the AI-commentary '3-layer chain' error sat undetected through rounds 1-6 and only surfaced in r7; a 'clean' round only means 'this sample found nothing', never 'nothing exists'). (2) doc-fixes THEMSELVES introduce ~1 new error per few rounds (the r3 README commentary edit became an r7 WRONG). So a full sweep can never PROVE 0; it can only lower the expected count. Recurring non-doc sources cleared: clap help strings (r4, code). Version/tag drift disclosed (tag NOT created — triggers release.yml). PRAGMATIC STOPPING RULE: run a full sweep periodically (>30d) and after big changes; fix what it finds; do NOT loop-to-zero (it doesn't terminate). Per-diff scoped runs are the cheap routine guard.
